name: 34 Street FPS §5.12 traffic safety & mobility review — real CA planning-stage issue/response pair (Strathcona County)

metadata.name: 34 Street Functional Planning Study — Traffic Safety Audit & Mobility Review
metadata.description: Real planning-stage safety review embedded in the 34 Street Functional Planning Study (Strathcona County with City of Edmonton, 2013): auditor issue list plus designer's response table (Table 5-1), with Appendix H audited alignment sheets as inputs companion (sample CA-011). Converted from the published final report.
metadata.scheme_summary: Corridor upgrade concept for 34 Street: added travel lanes and turn bays, shared-use path along the corridor, ramp/intersection reconfigurations between Sherwood Park Freeway and Baseline Road.
metadata.authority: Strathcona County Transportation Planning & Engineering (with City of Edmonton)
metadata.location: 34 Street corridor, Edmonton / Strathcona County, Alberta

design_criteria.value: Recommended concept plan and profiles for 34 Street (May 2013) reviewed via plan mark-ups; Alberta practice lineage with City of Edmonton protected-prohibited dual-left phasing practice cited.

route_choice_project_scope.value: Corridor upgrade scope: travel lanes through the corridor and turn bays at intersections; shared-use path along the entire corridor; 78 Avenue right-in/right-out conversion; signalized WB-NB ramp intersection at Sherwood Park Freeway.

access_management_adjacent_developments.value: Private accesses along the corridor addressed in review findings on permissive left turns across 3+ opposing lanes.

expected_findings_baseline.location: 34 Street corridor — private accesses and intersections
expected_findings_baseline.scenario: The review records corridor-wide collision risk from permissive left turns across three or more opposing lanes at private accesses and intersections, with risk dependent on left-turn and opposing volumes. Pedestrians and cyclists crossing or traveling along the multi-lane corridor share the conflict space created by those permissive turns, alongside vehicle occupants; protected-left phasing is flagged for consideration at later design stages or future operational phases.

statement.text: Carry forward protected-left-turn phasing analysis for accesses and intersections across 3+ opposing lanes into subsequent design stages of the 34 Street corridor upgrade.

evidence.quote: Risk of collisions due to permissive left turns across 3+ opposing lanes at private accesses and intersections along the corridor.
minimise potentially negative safety impacts both within and outside the project limits, i.e. to avoid introducing collisions elsewhere along the route or on the network.

confidence.label: high
confidence.basis: The permissive-left risk statement is recorded directly in the sample report's general concerns; volume-dependence phrasing preserved from the source.

expected_findings_baseline.rationale: ORCH-as-judge baseline derived from the recorded concern list; distinguishable from quoted evidence, which supplies the recorded mechanism.
expected_findings_baseline.recommendation: Evaluate protected-left-turn phasing need for accesses and intersections across 3+ opposing lanes during subsequent design stages, explicitly accounting for pedestrian and cyclist exposure at those conflict points.

expected_findings_baseline.scenario: The designer response table records a potentially discontinuous sidewalk at the new 33 Street connection, leaving pedestrian connections unconfirmed at a new junction of the upgraded corridor.

statement.text: Provide a continuous sidewalk through the new 33 Street connection when that junction is built, closing the recorded potential discontinuity.

evidence.quote: Potentially discontinuous sidewalk at new 33 Street connection.

confidence.label: high
confidence.basis: The discontinuity entry is recorded verbatim in Table 5-1 as an issue with designer response 'sidewalk connections to be confirmed at future design stages'.

expected_findings_baseline.rationale: ORCH-as-judge baseline framed as a compliance/continuity question because the sample itself defers confirmation to future design stages rather than asserting a hazard.
expected_findings_baseline.recommendation: Provide a continuous sidewalk connection through the new 33 Street junction in future design stages, resolving the recorded discontinuity rather than deferring it unbounded.
